title.zh: 卷三百三十一 列傳第二百十九 西域三
title.raw: 卷三百三十一 列傳第二百十九 西域三 Volume 331 Biographies 219: Western Regions 3

sentences.zh: 烏斯藏大寶法王

translations.literal: U-Tsang, the Great Precious Dharma King
translations.idiomatic: The Great Precious Dharma King of U-Tsang

sentences.zh: 烏斯藏，在雲南西徼外，去雲南麗江府千余里，四川馬湖府千五百余里，陝西西寧衛五千余里。

translations.literal: U-Tsang lies beyond the western frontier of Yunnan, more than a thousand li from Lijiang Prefecture in Yunnan, more than fifteen hundred li from Mahu Prefecture in Sichuan, and more than five thousand li from Xining Guard in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: U-Tsang lay beyond Yunnan's western marches, over a thousand li from Lijiang Prefecture, fifteen hundred li from Mahu Prefecture in Sichuan, and five thousand li from Xining Guard in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 其地多僧，無城郭。

translations.literal: That land has many monks and no walled towns.
translations.idiomatic: The region was thick with monks and had no walled towns.

sentences.zh: 群居大土臺上，不食肉娶妻，無刑罰，亦無兵革，鮮疾病。

translations.literal: They dwell together on great earthen platforms, eat no meat, take wives, have no punishments, have no warfare, and seldom suffer illness.
translations.idiomatic: People lived together on great earthen platforms, abstained from meat yet married, knew neither punishments nor warfare, and rarely fell ill.

sentences.zh: 佛書甚多，《楞伽經》至萬卷。

translations.literal: Buddhist texts are very numerous; the Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra alone runs to ten thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhist scriptures were abundant; the Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra alone ran to ten thousand scrolls.

sentences.zh: 其土台外，僧有食肉娶妻者。

translations.literal: Outside those platforms, some monks eat meat and take wives.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond those platforms, some monks ate meat and took wives.

sentences.zh: 元世祖尊八思巴為大寶法王，錫玉印，既沒，賜號皇天之下一人之上宣文輔治大聖至德普覺真智佐國如意大寶法王西天佛子大元帝師。

translations.literal: The Yuan founder honored 'Phags-pa as Great Precious Dharma King and bestowed a jade seal; after his death he was granted the title, under Heaven and above the One Man, of Xuanwen Fuzhi Great Sage, Perfect Virtue, Universal Enlightenment, True Wisdom, State-Assisting, As-You-Will Great Precious Dharma King, Buddha Son of the Western Heaven, Imperial Preceptor of the Great Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai honored 'Phags-pa as Great Precious Dharma King and gave him a jade seal; after his death he was posthumously titled, beneath Heaven and above all others, Xuanwen Fuzhi Great Sage of perfect virtue and universal enlightenment, true wisdom aiding the state, Great Precious Dharma King, Buddha Son of the Western Heaven, and Imperial Preceptor of the Great Yuan.

sentences.zh: 自是，其徒嗣者咸稱帝師。

translations.literal: From then on, his successors in the lineage were all called Imperial Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter every successor in his line was styled Imperial Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，太祖懲唐世吐蕃之亂，思制御之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongwu, the Founder, mindful of the Tang-era turmoil caused by Tibet, thought to control it.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Hongwu reign the Founder, recalling the Tang-era chaos wrought by Tibet, sought to bring the region under control.

sentences.zh: 惟因其俗尚，用僧徒化導為善，乃遣使廣行招諭。

translations.literal: He only followed their customs, using monks to guide them toward goodness, and therefore sent envoys far and wide to summon and instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: He relied instead on local custom, using monks to lead people toward virtue, and sent envoys throughout the region to win them over.

sentences.zh: 又遣陝西行省員外郎許允德使其地，令舉元故官赴京授職。

translations.literal: He also sent Xu Yunde, an outside secretary of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, to that region with orders to recommend former Yuan officials to come to the capital and receive posts.
translations.idiomatic: He also dispatched Xu Yunde, an outside secretary of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, to recommend former Yuan officials for appointment at court.

sentences.zh: 於是烏斯藏攝帝師喃加巴藏卜先遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Thereupon the U-Tsang Regent Imperial Preceptor Namgyel Pakzangpo first sent envoys to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The U-Tsang Regent Imperial Preceptor Namgyel Pakzangpo then sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 五年十二月至京。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fifth year they reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: They reached the capital in the twelfth month of the fifth year.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，賜紅綺禪衣及鞋帽錢物。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and granted red silk monastic robes, shoes, caps, money, and goods.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and rewarded them with red silk monastic robes, footwear, caps, money, and other gifts.

sentences.zh: 明年二月躬自入朝，上所舉故官六十人。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year he came in person to court and presented the sixty former officials he had recommended.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the second month, he came to court in person and presented the sixty former officials he had recommended.

sentences.zh: 帝悉授以職，改攝帝師為熾盛佛寶國師，仍錫玉印及彩幣表裡各二十。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed them all to office, changed the Regent Imperial Preceptor's title to Blazing Buddha-Treasure State Preceptor, and again bestowed a jade seal and twenty sets of patterned silks, inner and outer.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed them all, renamed the Regent Imperial Preceptor Blazing Buddha-Treasure State Preceptor, and again gave him a jade seal plus twenty sets of patterned silks, inner and outer.

sentences.zh: 玉人制印成，帝眎玉未美，令更制，其崇敬如此。

translations.literal: When the jade craftsman finished the seal, the emperor saw that the stone was not fine enough and ordered it remade—such was the degree of his reverence.
translations.idiomatic: When the jade seal was finished the emperor found the stone inferior and ordered it remade—such was the esteem in which he held him.

sentences.zh: 暨辭還，命河州衛遣官齎敕偕行，招諭諸番之未附者。

translations.literal: When he took leave to return, the emperor ordered Hezhou Guard to send an officer bearing an imperial letter to travel with him and summon those western peoples not yet submitted.
translations.idiomatic: On his departure the emperor ordered an officer from Hezhou Guard to accompany him with an imperial letter summoning tribes still outside the fold.

sentences.zh: 冬，元帝師之後鎖南堅巴藏卜、元國公哥列思監藏巴藏卜並遣使乞玉印。

translations.literal: In winter, Suonan Jianbazangpo, descendant of the Yuan Imperial Preceptor, and the Yuan State Duke Gele Sijianzang Bazangpo both sent envoys begging for jade seals.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Suonan Jianbazangpo, heir of the Yuan Imperial Preceptor, and the Yuan State Duke Gele Sijianzang Bazangpo each sent envoys requesting jade seals.

sentences.zh: 廷臣言已嘗給賜，不宜復予，乃以文綺賜之。

translations.literal: Court officials said seals had already been granted and should not be given again; they were therefore rewarded with patterned silks.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials argued that jade seals had already been granted and should not be issued again, so they received patterned silks instead.

sentences.zh: 七年夏，佛寶國師遣其徒來貢。

translations.literal: In the summer of the seventh year the Buddha-Treasure State Preceptor sent his disciples to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the seventh year the Buddha-Treasure State Preceptor sent disciples with tribute.

sentences.zh: 秋，元帝師八思巴之後公哥監藏巴藏卜及烏斯藏僧答力麻八剌遣使來朝，請封號。

translations.literal: In autumn, Gongge Jianzang Bazangpo, descendant of the Yuan Imperial Preceptor 'Phags-pa, and the U-Tsang monk Daliba, sent envoys to court requesting enfeoffment titles.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Gongge Jianzang Bazangpo, heir of 'Phags-pa, and the U-Tsang monk Daliba sent envoys to court seeking enfeoffment titles.

sentences.zh: 詔授帝師後人為圓智妙覺弘教大國師，烏斯藏僧為灌頂國師，並賜玉印。

translations.literal: An edict appointed the Imperial Preceptor's descendant as Great State Preceptor of Perfect Wisdom and Subtle Enlightenment, Promoting the Teaching, and the U-Tsang monk as Abhiseka State Preceptor, and bestowed jade seals on both.
translations.idiomatic: An edict named the Imperial Preceptor's heir Great State Preceptor of Perfect Wisdom and Subtle Enlightenment, Promoting the Teaching, and the U-Tsang monk Abhiseka State Preceptor, each receiving a jade seal.

sentences.zh: 佛寶國師復遣其徒來貢，上所舉土官五十八人，亦皆授職。

translations.literal: The Buddha-Treasure State Preceptor again sent disciples to offer tribute; the fifty-eight native officials he presented were all granted office.
translations.idiomatic: The Buddha-Treasure State Preceptor again sent tribute, and all fifty-eight native officials he recommended were appointed.

sentences.zh: 九年，答力麻八剌遣使來貢。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Daliba sent envoys to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Daliba sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 十一年復貢，奏舉故官十六人為宣慰、招討等官，亦皆報允。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year they offered tribute again and memorialized recommending sixteen former officials as pacification commissioners, bandit-suppression commissioners, and the like; all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: They came again in the eleventh year, recommending sixteen former officials as pacification and bandit-suppression commissioners; all were approved.

sentences.zh: 十四年復貢。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year they offered tribute again.
translations.idiomatic: They sent tribute again in the fourteenth year.

sentences.zh: 帝將薦福於高帝後，命建普度大齋於靈谷寺七日。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to pray for blessings on behalf of the late Founder and ordered a seven-day universal salvation great ritual held at Linggu Temple.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor wished to pray for blessings on behalf of the late Founder, he ordered a seven-day universal salvation ritual at Linggu Temple.

sentences.zh: 帝躬自行香。

translations.literal: The emperor personally went to burn incense.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went in person to burn incense.

sentences.zh: 於是卿雲、甘露、青烏、白象之屬，連日畢見。

translations.literal: Thereupon auspicious clouds, sweet dew, blue birds, white elephants, and the like appeared day after day.
translations.idiomatic: Auspicious clouds, sweet dew, blue birds, white elephants, and the like then appeared for days on end.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，侍臣多獻賦頌。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, and many attending officials presented rhapsodies and eulogies.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, and many courtiers presented laudatory verse.

sentences.zh: 事竣，復賜黃金百，白金千，寶鈔二千，彩幣表裡百二十，馬九。

translations.literal: When the rite ended he again bestowed one hundred taels of gold, one thousand taels of silver, two thousand notes of treasure paper, one hundred twenty sets of patterned silks inner and outer, and nine horses.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite ended he again gave one hundred taels of gold, one thousand of silver, two thousand treasure notes, one hundred twenty sets of patterned silks, and nine horses.

sentences.zh: 其徒灌頂圓通善慧大國師答師巴羅葛羅思等，亦加優賜。

translations.literal: His disciples, including the Abhiseka All-Pervading Good-Wisdom Great State Preceptor Dashi Baroluo Geluosi, also received generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: His disciples, including the Abhiseka All-Pervading Good-Wisdom Great State Preceptor Dashi Baroluo Geluosi, received generous gifts as well.

sentences.zh: 遂封哈立麻為萬行具足十方最勝圓覺妙智慧善普應佑國演教如來大寶法王西天大善自在佛，領天下釋教，賜印誥及金、銀、鈔、彩幣、織金珠袈裟、金銀器、鞍馬。

translations.literal: Halima was then enfeoffed as Great Precious Dharma King, Tathāgata of Ten Thousand Perfect Practices, Complete in the Ten Directions, Supreme Perfect Enlightenment, Subtle Wisdom, Good Universal Response, State-Protecting, Teaching-Expounding, Great Good Self-Master Buddha of the Western Heaven, put in charge of the Buddhist clergy throughout the realm, and granted patent of appointment, gold, silver, notes, patterned silks, gold-brocade pearl kasāya, gold and silver vessels, and saddled horses.
translations.idiomatic: Halima was then enfeoffed Great Precious Dharma King, Tathāgata of perfect practice and supreme enlightenment, protector of the state and expounder of the teaching, Great Good Self-Master Buddha of the Western Heaven, placed over the Buddhist clergy empire-wide, and given patent, gold, silver, notes, silks, brocade kasāya, vessels, and horses.

sentences.zh: 命其徒孛隆逋瓦桑兒加領真為灌頂圓修淨慧大國師，高日瓦禪伯為灌頂通悟弘濟大國師，果欒羅葛羅監藏巴裡藏卜為灌頂弘智淨戒大國師，並賜印誥、銀鈔、彩幣。

translations.literal: His disciple Belongpo Wasang'er Jialingzhen was appointed Abhiseka Perfect-Practice Pure-Wisdom Great State Preceptor; Gaoriwa Chanbo, Abhiseka Penetrating-Enlightenment Great-Benefit Great State Preceptor; and Guoluoluo Geluo Jianzang Balizangbu, Abhiseka Expansive-Wisdom Pure-Discipline Great State Preceptor; each received patent, silver notes, and patterned silks.
translations.idiomatic: His disciples Belongpo Wasang'er Jialingzhen, Gaoriwa Chanbo, and Guoluoluo Geluo Jianzang Balizangbu were named Abhiseka Great State Preceptors of pure wisdom, penetrating enlightenment, and expansive wisdom respectively, each receiving patent, silver notes, and silks.

sentences.zh: 已，命哈立麻赴五台山建大齋，再為高帝後薦福，賜予優厚。

translations.literal: Afterward Halima was ordered to Mount Wutai to hold a great ritual and again pray for blessings for the late Founder; the gifts were lavish.
translations.idiomatic: Halima was then sent to Mount Wutai for another great ritual on the Founder's behalf and rewarded even more generously.

sentences.zh: 六年四月辭歸，復賜金幣、佛像，命中官護行。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the sixth year he took leave to return; he was again given gold coins and Buddha images, and a eunuch was ordered to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: He left in the fourth month of the sixth year with more gold and Buddha images, escorted by a eunuch.

sentences.zh: 自是，迄正統末，入貢者八。

translations.literal: From then until the end of the Zhengtong reign tribute missions came eight times.
translations.idiomatic: From then until the end of Zhengtong there were eight tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 已，法王卒，久不奉貢。

translations.literal: Afterward the Dharma King died and for a long time no tribute was sent.
translations.idiomatic: After the Dharma King died tribute ceased for many years.

sentences.zh: 弘治八年，王葛哩麻巴始遣使來貢。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Hongzhi, King Geleima Ba first sent envoys to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 8 King Geleima Ba sent envoys with tribute for the first time.

sentences.zh: 十二年兩貢，禮官以一歲再貢非制，請裁其賜賚，從之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year they offered tribute twice; ritual officials said two missions in one year were against regulation and asked that rewards be reduced; the request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: They came twice in the twelfth year; ritual officials held that two missions in one year violated precedent and secured a cut in rewards.

sentences.zh: 正德元年來貢。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengde they came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: They sent tribute in the first year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 十年復來貢。

translations.literal: In the tenth year they came again to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: They came again in the tenth year.

sentences.zh: 時帝惑近習言，謂烏斯藏僧有能知三生者，國人稱之為活佛，欣然欲見之。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor, misled by favorites, was told that a U-Tsang monk could know the three lives; his countrymen called him the Living Buddha, and the emperor eagerly wished to see him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, swayed by favorites, heard that a U-Tsang monk could know past, present, and future lives; his people called him the Living Buddha, and the emperor was eager to meet him.

sentences.zh: 考永、宣間陳誠、侯顯入番故事，命中官劉允乘傳往迎。

translations.literal: Reviewing the Yongle and Xuande precedents of Chen Cheng and Hou Xian entering the western regions, he ordered the eunuch Liu Yun to travel by relay post to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Citing Yongle and Xuande precedents when Chen Cheng and Hou Xian went west, he ordered the eunuch Liu Yun to travel by relay post to bring the monk in.

sentences.zh: 閣臣梁儲等言：「西番之教，邪妄不經。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Liang Chu and others said: "The religion of the western Tibetans is heterodox, delusive, and unorthodox.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Liang Chu and others said, "The faith of the western Tibetans is heterodox and unorthodox.

sentences.zh: 我祖宗朝雖嘗遣使，蓋因天下初定，藉以化導愚頑，鎮撫荒服，非信其教而崇奉之也。

translations.literal: Although our founding ancestors sometimes sent envoys, it was because the realm had just been pacified and they wished to use it to guide the foolish and stubborn and soothe the remote borderlands—not because they believed the religion and honored it.
translations.idiomatic: Our founders sent envoys only because the realm was newly settled, to guide the stubborn and pacify distant tribes—not because they believed or revered the faith.

sentences.zh: 承平之後，累朝列聖止因其來朝而賞賚之，未嘗輕辱命使，遠涉其地。

translations.literal: After peace was secured, successive sage emperors only rewarded them when they came to court and never lightly sent commissioned envoys to travel far into their lands.
translations.idiomatic: In later peaceful reigns successive emperors merely rewarded those who came to court and never lightly sent envoys deep into their country.

sentences.zh: 今忽遣近侍往送幢幡，朝野聞之，莫不駭愕。

translations.literal: Now you suddenly send a close attendant to deliver banners and canopies; when court and commoners hear of it, none are not appalled.
translations.idiomatic: Now you suddenly send a close attendant with banners and canopies; court and country are alike appalled.

sentences.zh: 而允奏乞鹽引至數萬，動撥馬船至百艘，又許其便宜處置錢物，勢必攜帶私鹽，騷擾郵傳，為官民患。

translations.literal: Moreover Yun memorialized begging salt certificates to the tens of thousands, requisitioning transport boats by the hundred, and was allowed to dispose of money and goods at his discretion; he would surely carry private salt, harass the postal routes, and become a plague to officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: Yun moreover asked for tens of thousands of salt certificates, commandeered up to a hundred transport boats, and was allowed to spend funds at will—he would surely smuggle salt, harass the post roads, and afflict officials and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 今蜀中大盜初平，瘡痍未起。

translations.literal: Now the great bandits of Shu have only just been pacified and the wounds are not yet healed.
translations.idiomatic: The great Shu rebellions have only just been crushed and the region is still devastated.

sentences.zh: 在官已無余積，必至苛斂軍民，釒廷而走險，盜將復發。

translations.literal: The government already has no surplus; harsh levies on soldiers and civilians are inevitable, and they will flee to desperate courses—bandits will rise again.
translations.idiomatic: Official coffers are empty; harsh levies will drive soldiers and civilians to desperate courses and banditry will return.

sentences.zh: 況自天全六番出境，涉數萬之程，曆數歲之久，道途絕無郵置，人馬安從供頓？

translations.literal: Moreover, from leaving the Six Tianshan Pacification Commissions one must travel tens of thousands of li over several years; on the road there are absolutely no postal stations—how are men and horses to be supplied?
translations.idiomatic: From the Six Tianshan pacification districts the journey runs tens of thousands of li over years with no postal stations—how are men and horses to be fed?

sentences.zh: 脫中途遇寇，何以御之？

translations.literal: If bandits are met on the way, how will they be resisted?
translations.idiomatic: If bandits strike on the road, how will they be resisted?

sentences.zh: 虧中國之體，納外番之侮，無一可者。

translations.literal: It diminishes the dignity of China and invites insult from foreign tribes—there is not one point in its favor.
translations.idiomatic: It shames China and invites foreign contempt—not one point favors it.

sentences.zh: 所齎敕書，臣等不敢撰擬。」

translations.literal: As for the imperial letter to be carried, your ministers dare not draft it.
translations.idiomatic: We dare not draft the imperial letter he is to carry.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書毛紀、六科給事中葉相、十三道御史周倫等並切諫，亦不聽。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Mao Ji, supervising secretaries Ye Xiang of the Six Offices, Censor Zhou Lun of the Thirteen Circuits, and others all remonstrated urgently; he still would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Mao Ji, supervising secretaries, and censors all remonstrated urgently; he still refused.

sentences.zh: 允行，以珠琲為幢幡，黃金為供具，賜其僧金印，犒賞以鉅萬計，內庫黃金為之罄盡。

translations.literal: Yun set out, using pearl strings for banners and canopies and gold for ritual vessels; he was to bestow a gold seal on the monk, and rewards ran to vast sums—the inner treasury's gold was exhausted for it.
translations.idiomatic: Yun set out with pearl banners and gold ritual vessels, a gold seal for the monk, and rewards in the tens of thousands that emptied the inner treasury of gold.

sentences.zh: 敕允往返以十年為期，所攜茶鹽以數十萬計。

translations.literal: An edict fixed ten years for Yun's round trip; the tea and salt he carried were reckoned in the hundreds of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He was given ten years for the round trip and carried tea and salt reckoned in the hundreds of thousands.

sentences.zh: 允至臨清，漕艘為之阻滯。

translations.literal: When Yun reached Linqing, grain-transport boats were blocked on his account.
translations.idiomatic: At Linqing his passage blocked the grain fleet.

sentences.zh: 入峽江，舟大難進，易以冓鹿，相連二百余里。

translations.literal: Entering the gorges, the boats were too large to advance and were changed to rafts, linked for more than two hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: In the gorges the boats were too large to pass and were replaced with rafts strung together for over two hundred li.

sentences.zh: 及抵成都，日支官廩百石，蔬菜銀百兩，錦官驛不足，取傍近數十驛供之。

translations.literal: When he reached Chengdu, a hundred piculs of official grain and a hundred taels of silver for vegetables were spent daily; Jinguan Post Station was insufficient and several dozen nearby stations were used to supply him.
translations.idiomatic: At Chengdu he consumed a hundred piculs of official grain and a hundred taels of silver for vegetables daily; dozens of nearby post stations had to feed his party.

sentences.zh: 治入番器物，估直二十萬。

translations.literal: Preparing goods for entering the western regions was estimated at two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Outfitting the mission for Tibet was estimated at two hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 守臣力爭，減至十三萬。

translations.literal: The guarding officials argued strenuously and reduced it to one hundred thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials protested until the figure was cut to one hundred thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 工人雜造，夜以繼日。

translations.literal: Craftsmen of every sort worked day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Craftsmen worked day and night.

sentences.zh: 居歲餘，始率將校十人、士千人以行，越兩月入其地。

translations.literal: After more than a year he finally led ten officers and a thousand soldiers to set out; after two months they entered that region.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he set out with ten officers and a thousand men and entered Tibet two months later.

sentences.zh: 所謂活佛者，恐中國誘害之，匿不出見。

translations.literal: The so-called Living Buddha, fearing that China would lure and harm him, hid and would not appear.
translations.idiomatic: The Living Buddha, fearing Chinese treachery, hid and refused an audience.

sentences.zh: 將士怒，欲脅以威。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers were angry and wished to coerce him by force.
translations.idiomatic: The troops grew angry and wanted to coerce him by force.

sentences.zh: 番人夜襲之，奪寶貨、器械以去。

translations.literal: The western tribesmen attacked by night and carried off treasure and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Tibetans raided by night and made off with treasure and arms.

sentences.zh: 將校死者二人，卒數百人，傷者半之。

translations.literal: Two officers died, several hundred soldiers died, and half as many were wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Two officers and hundreds of soldiers were killed; half as many were wounded.

sentences.zh: 允乘善馬疾走，僅免。

translations.literal: Yun mounted a good horse and fled swiftly, barely escaping.
translations.idiomatic: Yun fled on a fast horse and barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 返成都，戒部下弗言，而以空函馳奏，至則武宗已崩。

translations.literal: Returning to Chengdu, he forbade his subordinates to speak of it and sent an urgent memorial in an empty case; when it arrived, Emperor Wuzong had already died.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Chengdu he silenced his men and sent an urgent report in an empty case; by the time it arrived Wuzong was dead.

sentences.zh: 世宗召允還，下吏治罪。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong summoned Yun back and handed him to the judicial authorities for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong recalled Yun and had him prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，法王猶數入貢，迄神宗朝不絕。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing era the Dharma King still sent tribute several times; down to the Shenzong reign it did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jiajing the Dharma King still sent tribute repeatedly, and missions continued through Shenzong's reign.

sentences.zh: 時有僧鎖南堅錯者，能知已往未來事，稱活佛，順義王俺答亦崇信之。

translations.literal: At that time there was a monk, Suonan Jianzang, who could know past and future events; he was called the Living Buddha, and the Shunyi Prince Altan also revered him.
translations.idiomatic: A monk named Suonan Jianzang, said to know past and future, was called the Living Buddha; the Shunyi Prince Altan revered him as well.

sentences.zh: 萬曆七年，以迎活佛為名，西侵瓦剌，為所敗。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Wanli, under the pretext of welcoming the Living Buddha, he invaded Oirat to the west and was defeated by them.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 7 Altan marched west against the Oirats in the name of escorting the Living Buddha and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 此僧戒以好殺，勸之東還。

translations.literal: This monk admonished him against love of killing and urged him to return east.
translations.idiomatic: The monk warned him against slaughter and urged him to turn back east.

sentences.zh: 俺答亦勸此僧通中國，乃自甘州遺書張居正，自稱釋迦摩尼比丘，求通貢，饋以儀物。

translations.literal: Altan also urged this monk to communicate with China; the monk then from Ganzhou sent a letter to Zhang Juzheng, calling himself a śramaṇa disciple of Śākyamuni, requesting permission to offer tribute, and presenting ritual gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Altan also urged the monk to open ties with China; from Ganzhou the monk wrote Zhang Juzheng, styling himself a disciple of Śākyamuni, seeking tribute rights and sending ritual gifts.

sentences.zh: 居正不敢受，聞之於帝。

translations.literal: Juzheng dared not accept them and reported to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng dared not accept the gifts and reported to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝命受之，而許其貢。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered that they be accepted and allowed his tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the gifts accepted and allowed tribute.

sentences.zh: 由是，中國亦知有活佛。

translations.literal: From this China also came to know of the Living Buddha.
translations.idiomatic: China thus learned of the Living Buddha.

sentences.zh: 此僧有異術能服人，諸番莫不從其教，即大寶法王及闡化諸王，亦皆俯首稱弟子。

translations.literal: This monk had strange arts by which he could subdue people; all the western tribes followed his teaching, and even the Great Precious Dharma King and the Taming Kings all bowed their heads and called themselves his disciples.
translations.idiomatic: The monk's uncanny powers won every tribe; even the Great Precious Dharma King and the Taming Kings bowed as his disciples.

sentences.zh: 自是西方止知奉此僧，諸番王徒擁虛位，不復能施其號令矣。

translations.literal: From then on the west knew only to serve this monk; the various tribal kings merely held empty titles and could no longer enforce their commands.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the west obeyed only this monk; tribal kings held empty titles and could no longer command.

sentences.zh: 大乘法王

translations.literal: The Mahāyāna Dharma King
translations.idiomatic: The Mahāyāna Dharma King

sentences.zh: 大乘法王者，烏斯藏僧昆澤思巴也，其徒亦稱為尚師。

translations.literal: The Mahāyāna Dharma King was the U-Tsang monk Kunzang Siba; his disciples also called him Revered Teacher.
translations.idiomatic: The Mahāyāna Dharma King was the U-Tsang monk Kunzang Siba, whom his disciples called Revered Teacher.

sentences.zh: 永樂時，成祖既封哈立麻，又聞昆澤思巴有道術，命中官齎璽書銀幣徵之。

translations.literal: In the Yongle era, after Chengzu had enfeoffed Halima, he also heard that Kunzang Siba possessed the Way and ordered a eunuch to carry an imperial letter and silver gifts to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: After enfeoffing Halima, Chengzu heard Kunzang Siba possessed spiritual arts and sent a eunuch with an imperial letter and silver to summon him.

sentences.zh: 其僧先遣人貢舍利、佛像，遂偕使者入朝。

translations.literal: The monk first sent men to offer relics and Buddha images, then accompanied the envoy to court.
translations.idiomatic: He first sent relics and Buddha images, then came to court with the envoy.

sentences.zh: 十一年二月至京，帝即延見，賜藏經、銀鈔、彩幣、鞍馬、茶果諸物，封為萬行圓融妙法最勝真如慧智弘慈廣濟護國演教正覺大乘法王西天上善金剛普應大光明佛，領天下釋教，賜印誥、袈裟、幡幢、鞍馬、傘器諸物，禮之亞於大寶法王。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eleventh year he reached the capital; the emperor immediately received him, granted canonical texts, silver notes, patterned silks, saddled horses, tea, fruit, and other goods, and enfeoffed him as Mahāyāna Dharma King, Perfectly Enlightened Buddha of Ten Thousand Perfect Practices, Harmonious Subtle Dharma, Supreme True Suchness, Wise Intelligence, Expansive Compassion, Broad Relief, State-Protecting, Teaching-Expanding, Superior Good Vajra of the Western Heaven, Universally Responding Great Brightness, put in charge of the Buddhist clergy throughout the realm, and granted patent, kasāya, banners, saddled horses, parasols, and other objects; he was honored second only to the Great Precious Dharma King.
translations.idiomatic: He reached the capital in the second month of the eleventh year, was received at once, and enfeoffed Mahāyāna Dharma King with patent, scriptures, silks, horses, and ritual gear, ranking just below the Great Precious Dharma King.

sentences.zh: 明年辭歸，賜加於前，命中官護行。

translations.literal: The next year he took leave to return; gifts were added to those before, and a eunuch was ordered to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he left with added gifts and a eunuch escort.

sentences.zh: 後數入貢，帝亦先後命中官喬來喜、楊三保齎賜佛像、法器、袈裟、禪衣、絨錦、彩幣諸物。

translations.literal: Later he offered tribute several times, and the emperor also successively ordered the eunuchs Qiao Laixi and Yang Sanbao to carry Buddha images, ritual implements, kasāya, monastic robes, velvet brocade, patterned silks, and other goods as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He sent tribute several times thereafter, and the emperor repeatedly dispatched eunuchs with Buddha images, ritual gear, robes, brocades, and silks.

sentences.zh: 洪熙、宣德間並來貢。

translations.literal: During Hongxi and Xuande he came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: He sent tribute during Hongxi and Xuande.

sentences.zh: 成化四年，其王完卜遣使來貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chenghua, his king Wanbu sent envoys to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 4 King Wanbu sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 禮官言無法王印文，且從洮州入，非制，宜減其賜物。

translations.literal: Ritual officials said there was no Dharma King seal document and that entering by Taozhou was against regulation; rewards should be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officials noted the lack of a Dharma King seal and entry via Taozhou contrary to precedent and urged reduced rewards.

sentences.zh: 使者言，所居去烏斯藏二十余程，涉五年方達京師，且所進馬多，乞給全賜，乃命量增。

translations.literal: The envoys said their residence was more than twenty stages from U-Tsang and took five years to reach the capital, and that the horses presented were many; they begged full reward, and an order was given to increase it proportionally.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys said they lived twenty stages from U-Tsang, took five years to reach the capital, and brought many horses; they were granted an increased reward.

sentences.zh: 十七年來貢。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year they came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: They came again in the seventeenth year.

sentences.zh: 弘治元年，其王桑加瓦遣使來貢。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongzhi, his king Sangjawa sent envoys to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 1 King Sangjawa sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 故事，法王卒，其徒自相繼承，不由朝命。

translations.literal: By precedent, when a Dharma King died his disciples succeeded one another on their own, without court appointment.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, when a Dharma King died his disciples succeeded one another without court appointment.

sentences.zh: 三年，輔教王遣使奉貢，奏舉大乘法王襲職。

translations.literal: In the third year the Assistant-Teaching King sent envoys with tribute and memorialized recommending succession to the Mahāyāna Dharma King's post.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the Assistant-Teaching King sent tribute and asked that the Mahāyāna Dharma King's post be inherited.

sentences.zh: 帝但納其貢，賜賚遣還，不命襲職。

translations.literal: The emperor only accepted the tribute, bestowed rewards, and sent them back, not ordering succession to office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted the tribute, rewarded them, and sent them home without confirming succession.

sentences.zh: 正德五年遣其徒綽吉我些兒等，從河州衛入貢。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengde he sent his disciples Chuoqi Wo'er and others to offer tribute by way of Hezhou Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 5 he sent his disciples Chuoqi Wo'er and others to offer tribute via Hezhou Guard.

sentences.zh: 禮官以其非貢道，請減其賞，並治指揮徐經罪，從之。

translations.literal: Ritual officials, because this was not the tribute route, asked that rewards be reduced and that Commander Xu Jing be punished; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officials said the route was improper, urged reduced rewards and punishment for Commander Xu Jing, and were heeded.

sentences.zh: 已，綽吉我些兒有寵於帝，亦封大德法王。

translations.literal: Later Chuoqi Wo'er won the emperor's favor and was also enfeoffed as Great Virtue Dharma King.
translations.idiomatic: Later Chuoqi Wo'er gained imperial favor and was enfeoffed Great Virtue Dharma King as well.

sentences.zh: 十年，僧完卜鎖南堅參巴爾藏卜遣使來貢，乞襲大乘法王。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the monk Wanbu Suonanjian Canba'er Zangbu sent envoys to offer tribute and begged to inherit the Mahāyāna Dharma King title.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Monk Wanbu Suonanjian Canba'er Zangbu sent tribute and asked to succeed as Mahāyāna Dharma King.

sentences.zh: 禮官失於稽考，竟許之。

translations.literal: Ritual officials failed in their investigation and ultimately allowed it.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officials failed to verify the claim and approved it anyway.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十五年偕輔教、闡教諸王來貢，使者至四千余人。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Jiajing he came to offer tribute together with the Assistant-Teaching and Propagation-Teaching kings, and the envoys numbered more than four thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 15 he came with the Assistant-Teaching and Propagation-Teaching kings, bringing more than four thousand envoys.

sentences.zh: 帝以人數逾額，減其賞，並治四川三司官濫送之罪。

translations.literal: Because the number exceeded the quota, the emperor reduced rewards and also punished officials of the three Sichuan commissions for sending them indiscriminately.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor cut rewards for exceeding the quota and punished Sichuan's three commissions for indiscriminate escort.

sentences.zh: 初，成祖封闡化等五王，各有分地，惟二法王以游僧不常厥居，故其貢期不在三年之列。

translations.literal: At first Chengzu enfeoffed the five Taming kings and others, each with his own domain; only the two Dharma Kings, as itinerant monks without fixed abodes, were not subject to the three-year tribute schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzu had enfeoffed the five Taming kings, each with a domain; only the two itinerant Dharma Kings stood outside the triennial tribute rule.

sentences.zh: 然終明世，奉貢不絕雲。

translations.literal: Yet throughout the Ming dynasty tribute was never cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Yet tribute continued without interruption throughout the Ming.

sentences.zh: 大慈法王

translations.literal: The Great Compassion Dharma King
translations.idiomatic: The Great Compassion Dharma King

sentences.zh: 大慈法王，名釋迦也失，亦烏斯藏僧稱為尚師者也。

translations.literal: The Great Compassion Dharma King was named Shakya Yeshe; he was also a U-Tsang monk whom people called Revered Teacher.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Compassion Dharma King was Shakya Yeshe, a U-Tsang monk whom western Tibetans called Revered Teacher.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，既封二法王，其徒爭欲見天子邀恩寵，於是來者趾相接。

translations.literal: During Yongle, after the two Dharma Kings had been enfeoffed, their disciples all competed to see the Son of Heaven and win favor, and arrivals followed one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: After Yongle enfeoffed the two Dharma Kings, their disciples vied to reach court for favor, and arrivals came in an unbroken stream.

sentences.zh: 釋迦也失亦以十二年入朝，禮亞大乘法王。

translations.literal: Shakya Yeshe also came to court in the twelfth year and was honored second only to the Mahāyāna Dharma King.
translations.idiomatic: Shakya Yeshe came to court in the twelfth year and ranked just below the Mahāyāna Dharma King.

sentences.zh: 明年命為妙覺圓通慈慧普應輔國顯教灌頂弘善西天佛子大國師，賜之印誥。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Marvelous Awakening, Perfectly Penetrating, Compassionate and Wise, Universally Responsive, State-Assisting, Teaching-Revealing, Abhisheka, Expansive Goodness, Buddha Son of the Western Heaven, Great State Teacher, and granted patent and commission.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was made Great State Teacher and Buddha Son of the Western Heaven with patent and commission.

sentences.zh: 十四年辭歸，賜佛經、佛像、法仗、僧衣、綺帛、金銀器，且御制贊詞賜之，其徒益以為榮。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he took leave to return; Buddhist scriptures, Buddha images, ritual implements, monastic robes, brocades, and gold and silver vessels were granted, and the emperor himself composed eulogies to bestow; his disciples took this as still greater honor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he left with scriptures, images, ritual gear, robes, silks, and gold and silver, plus imperial eulogies—his disciples counted it supreme honor.

sentences.zh: 明年遣使來貢。

translations.literal: The next year he sent envoys to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 十七年命中官楊三保齎佛像、衣幣往賜。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the emperor ordered the eunuch Yang Sanbao to carry Buddha images, robes, and silks as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year the eunuch Yang Sanbao was sent with Buddha images, robes, and silks.

sentences.zh: 二十一年復來貢。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year tribute came again.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute came again in the twenty-first year.

sentences.zh: 宣德九年入朝，帝留之京師，命成國公硃勇、禮部尚書胡濙持節，冊封為萬行妙明真如上勝清淨般若弘照普慧輔國顯教至善大慈法王西天正覺如來自在大圓通佛。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Xuande he came to court; the emperor kept him in the capital and ordered Duke of Chengguo Zhu Yong and Minister of Rites Hu Ying to bear credentials and enfeoff him as Buddha of Ten Thousand Perfect Practices, Subtle Brightness, Supreme True Suchness, Pure Prajñā, Expansive Illumination, Universal Wisdom, State-Assisting, Teaching-Revealing, Supreme Goodness, Great Compassion Dharma King, Perfectly Enlightened Tathāgata of the Western Heaven, Self-Existent Great Perfect Penetration.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 9 he came to court, was kept in the capital, and enfeoffed Great Compassion Dharma King by Duke of Chengguo Zhu Yong and Minister of Rites Hu Ying bearing credentials.

sentences.zh: 宣宗崩，英宗嗣位，禮官先奏汰番僧六百九十人，正統元年復以為請。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong died and Yingzong succeeded, ritual officials first memorialized to dismiss six hundred ninety Tibetan monks; in the first year of Zhengtong they asked again.
translations.idiomatic: After Xuanzong's death Yingzong's ritual officials first asked to dismiss 690 Tibetan monks and renewed the request in Zhengtong 1.

sentences.zh: 命大慈法王及西天佛子如故，余遣還，不願者減酒饌廩餼，自是輦下稍清。

translations.literal: The Great Compassion Dharma King and the Buddha Son of the Western Heaven were ordered to remain as before; the rest were sent back, and those unwilling to leave had wine, food, and stipends reduced; from then on the capital grew somewhat quieter.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Compassion Dharma King and the Buddha Son of the Western Heaven were kept; the rest were sent home, with reduced rations for those who refused, and the capital grew quieter.

sentences.zh: 西天佛子者，能仁寺僧智光也，本山東慶雲人。

translations.literal: The Buddha Son of the Western Heaven was Zhiguang, a monk of Nengren Temple, originally a native of Qingyun in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: The Buddha Son of the Western Heaven was Nengren Temple monk Zhiguang, a native of Qingyun in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 洪武、永樂中，數奉使西國。

translations.literal: During Hongwu and Yongle he was repeatedly sent as envoy to western lands.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu and Yongle he made repeated missions to the western regions.

sentences.zh: 成祖賜號國師，仁宗加號圓融妙慧淨覺弘濟輔國光范演教灌頂廣善大國師，賜金印、冠服、金銀器。

translations.literal: Chengzu granted him the title State Teacher; Renzong added the title Harmonious Subtle Wisdom, Pure Awakening, Expansive Relief, State-Assisting, Radiant Model, Teaching-Expanding, Abhisheka, Broad Goodness, Great State Teacher, and bestowed a gold seal, cap and robes, and gold and silver vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzu made him State Teacher; Renzong added Great State Teacher and gave a gold seal, robes, and gold and silver vessels.

sentences.zh: 至是復加西天佛子。

translations.literal: At this time he was further granted the title Buddha Son of the Western Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He was now further made Buddha Son of the Western Heaven.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖招徠番僧，本藉以化愚俗，弭邊患，授國師、大國師者不過四五人。

translations.literal: At first the Founder summoned Tibetan monks chiefly to transform ignorant custom and quell border troubles; those granted State Teacher or Great State Teacher numbered no more than four or five.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder first summoned Tibetan monks to guide the ignorant and pacify the frontier; only four or five received State Teacher or Great State Teacher titles.

sentences.zh: 至成祖兼崇其教，自闡化等五王及二法王外，授西天佛子者二，灌頂大國師者九，灌頂國師者十有八，其他禪師、僧官不可悉數。

translations.literal: By Chengzu's time the faith was also honored; apart from the five Taming kings and the two Dharma Kings, two were granted Buddha Son of the Western Heaven, nine Abhisheka Great State Teacher, eighteen Abhisheka State Teacher, and other Chan masters and monastic offices beyond full count.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chengzu the faith was also exalted: besides the five Taming kings and two Dharma Kings, two became Buddha Sons of the Western Heaven, nine Abhisheka Great State Teachers, eighteen Abhisheka State Teachers, and countless other Chan masters and monastic offices.

sentences.zh: 其徒交錯於道，外擾郵傳，內耗大官，公私騷然，帝不恤也。

translations.literal: Their disciples crisscrossed the roads, harassing the postal routes without and draining the Court of Imperial Entertainments within; public and private affairs were in turmoil, yet the emperor paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Their disciples clogged the roads, harassed the post routes, and drained the Court of Imperial Entertainments; public and private life were in turmoil, yet the emperor paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 然至者猶即遣還。

translations.literal: Yet those who arrived were still sent back at once.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, arrivals were still promptly sent home.

sentences.zh: 及宣宗時則久留京師，耗費益甚。

translations.literal: By Xuande's time they stayed long in the capital and expense grew still greater.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xuande they lingered in the capital and costs rose sharply.

sentences.zh: 英宗初年，雖多遣斥，其後加封號者亦不少。

translations.literal: In Yingzong's early years many were dismissed, yet afterward those granted new titles were also not few.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong dismissed many at first, but later still granted many new titles.

sentences.zh: 景泰中，封番僧沙加為弘慈大善法王，班卓兒藏卜為灌頂大國師。

translations.literal: During Jingtai the Tibetan monk Shajia was enfeoffed as Expansive Compassion, Great Goodness Dharma King, and Banzhuo'er Zangbu as Abhisheka Great State Teacher.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingtai reign Monk Shajia was made Expansive Compassion Great Goodness Dharma King and Banzhuo'er Zangbu Abhisheka Great State Teacher.

sentences.zh: 英宗復辟，務反景帝之政，降法王為大國師，大國師為國師。

translations.literal: When Yingzong restored the throne he set himself to reverse the Jing Emperor's policies, demoting Dharma Kings to Great State Teacher and Great State Teachers to State Teacher.
translations.idiomatic: On Yingzong's restoration he reversed the Jing Emperor's policies, demoting Dharma Kings to Great State Teacher and Great State Teachers to State Teacher.

sentences.zh: 成化初，憲宗復好番僧，至者日眾。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua Xianzong again favored Tibetan monks, and arrivals daily multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chenghua Xianzong again favored Tibetan monks, and arrivals swelled daily.

sentences.zh: 答刂巴堅參、答刂實巴、領占竹等，以秘密教得幸，並封法王。

translations.literal: Dali Bakyancan, Dali Shiba, Lingzhan Zhu, and others won favor through the Esoteric Teaching and were all enfeoffed as Dharma Kings.
translations.idiomatic: Dali Bakyancan, Dali Shiba, Lingzhan Zhu, and others won favor through Esoteric Buddhism and were all enfeoffed Dharma Kings.

sentences.zh: 其次為西天佛子，他授大國師、國師、禪師者不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Next came Buddha Sons of the Western Heaven; others granted Great State Teacher, State Teacher, or Chan master titles were beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Buddha Sons of the Western Heaven; Great State Teachers, State Teachers, and Chan masters were beyond count.

sentences.zh: 四方奸民投為弟子，輒得食大官，每歲耗費鉅萬。

translations.literal: Wicked men from all quarters enrolled as disciples and at once received food from the Court of Imperial Entertainments; each year the cost ran to tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Schemers from every quarter became disciples and fed at the Court of Imperial Entertainments at a cost of tens of thousands each year.

sentences.zh: 廷臣屢以為言，悉拒不聽。

translations.literal: Court ministers repeatedly spoke of it, but all were refused and he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers remonstrated repeatedly, but he refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 孝宗踐阼，清汰番僧，法王、佛子以下，皆遞降，驅還本土，奪其印誥，由是輦下復清。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong ascended the throne he purged Tibetan monks; from Dharma King and Buddha Son downward all were demoted in succession, driven back to their native lands, and stripped of patents and commissions; the capital thus grew quiet again.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong purged Tibetan monks, demoting Dharma Kings and Buddha Sons, sending them home and stripping patents; the capital grew quiet again.

sentences.zh: 弘治六年，帝惑近習言，命取領占竹等詣京。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Hongzhi the emperor, misled by close attendants, ordered Lingzhan Zhu and others brought to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 6, swayed by close attendants, the emperor ordered Lingzhan Zhu and others brought to court.

sentences.zh: 言官交章力諫，事乃寢。

translations.literal: Censorial officials submitted memorial after memorial in strong remonstrance, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Censors remonstrated in force, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 十三年命為故西天佛子著癿領占建塔。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he ordered a pagoda built for the late Buddha Son of the Western Heaven Zhuxiang Qu Lingzhan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he ordered a pagoda built for the late Buddha Son of the Western Heaven Zhuxiang Qu Lingzhan.

sentences.zh: 工部尚書徐貫等言，此僧無益於國，營墓足矣，不當建塔，不從。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Xu Guan and others said this monk had done the state no good; a tomb would suffice and a pagoda should not be built; he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Xu Guan argued the monk had served the state ill and a tomb would suffice; the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 尋命那卜堅參三人為灌頂大國師。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he appointed Napo Jancan and two others Abhisheka Great State Teachers.
translations.idiomatic: He soon made Napo Jancan and two others Abhisheka Great State Teachers.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，禮官請黜異教，三人並降禪師。

translations.literal: When the emperor died ritual officials asked that heterodox teachings be dismissed, and all three were demoted to Chan master.
translations.idiomatic: After his death ritual officials asked to purge heterodox faiths, and all three were demoted to Chan master.

sentences.zh: 既而武宗蠱惑佞幸，復取領占竹至京，命為灌頂大國師，以先所降禪師三人為國師。

translations.literal: Then Wuzong, deluded by flatterers, again brought Lingzhan Zhu to the capital, appointed him Abhisheka Great State Teacher, and made the three previously demoted Chan masters State Teachers.
translations.idiomatic: Then Wuzong, deluded by favorites, recalled Lingzhan Zhu, made him Abhisheka Great State Teacher, and restored the three demoted Chan masters as State Teachers.

sentences.zh: 帝好習番語，引入豹房，由是番僧復盛。

translations.literal: The emperor loved to study Tibetan language and brought them into the Leopard Quarter; Tibetan monks thus flourished again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor studied Tibetan, brought monks into the Leopard Quarter, and Tibetan influence revived.

sentences.zh: 封那卜堅參及答刂巴藏卜為法王，那卜領占及綽即羅竹為西天佛子。

translations.literal: Napo Jancan and Dali Bazangbu were enfeoffed as Dharma Kings; Napo Lingzhan and Chuoqi Luozhu as Buddha Sons of the Western Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Napo Jancan and Dali Bazangbu were made Dharma Kings; Napo Lingzhan and Chuoqi Luozhu Buddha Sons of the Western Heaven.

sentences.zh: 已，封領占班丹為大慶法王，給番僧度牒三千，聽其自度。

translations.literal: Later Lingzhan Bandan was enfeoffed as Great Celebration Dharma King; three thousand ordination certificates were given to Tibetan monks, and they were allowed to ordain one another.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhan Bandan was then made Great Celebration Dharma King; three thousand ordination certificates were issued and Tibetan monks allowed to ordain one another.

sentences.zh: 或言，大慶法王，即帝自號也。

translations.literal: Some said the Great Celebration Dharma King was in fact the emperor's own assumed title.
translations.idiomatic: Some said the Great Celebration Dharma King was the emperor's own assumed title.

sentences.zh: 綽吉我些兒者，烏斯藏使臣，留豹房有寵，封大德法王。

translations.literal: Chuoqi Wo'er was a U-Tsang envoy who stayed in the Leopard Quarter, won favor, and was enfeoffed as Great Virtue Dharma King.
translations.idiomatic: Chuoqi Wo'er was a U-Tsang envoy who lived in the Leopard Quarter, won favor, and was made Great Virtue Dharma King.

sentences.zh: 乞令其徒二人為正副使，還居本土，如大乘法王例入貢，且為二人請國師誥命，入番設茶。

translations.literal: He begged that two of his disciples be made chief and deputy envoys, return to dwell in their native land, offer tribute as the Mahāyāna Dharma King did, and also asked patents of State Teacher commission for the two and permission to establish tea distribution among the tribes.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that two disciples serve as chief and deputy envoys at home, offer tribute like the Mahāyāna Dharma King, receive State Teacher patents, and establish tea trade among the tribes.

sentences.zh: 禮官劉春等執不可，帝不聽。

translations.literal: Ritual officials Liu Chun and others insisted it could not be done; the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officials Liu Chun and others objected, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 春等復言：「烏斯藏遠在西方，性極頑獷。

translations.literal: Liu Chun and others again said: "U-Tsang lies far in the west and by nature is extremely stubborn and fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chun and others again said, "U-Tsang lies far in the west and is by nature stubborn and fierce.

sentences.zh: 雖設四王撫化，而其來貢必為節制。

translations.literal: Although four kings were established to soothe and transform them, their tribute missions must be regulated.
translations.idiomatic: Though four kings were set to pacify them, tribute missions must be strictly regulated.

sentences.zh: 若令齎茶以往，賜之誥命，彼或假上旨以誘諸番，妄有所干請。

translations.literal: If they are allowed to carry tea there and are granted commissions, they may borrow imperial authority to entice the tribes and presumptuously make requests.
translations.idiomatic: If they carry tea westward with imperial patents, they may abuse imperial authority to entice the tribes and make reckless demands.

sentences.zh: 從之則非法，不從則生釁，害不可勝言。」

translations.literal: To grant such requests would violate law; to refuse would breed conflict; the harm cannot be fully told.
translations.idiomatic: To grant such requests would break the law; to refuse would breed conflict—the harm is incalculable.

sentences.zh: 帝乃罷設茶敕，而予之誥命。

translations.literal: The emperor then revoked the tea-establishment edict but granted the commissions.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor revoked the tea-establishment edict but granted the patents.

sentences.zh: 帝時益好異教，常服其服，誦習其經，演法內廠。

translations.literal: The emperor then favored heterodox teachings still more, often wore their robes, recited their scriptures, and preached the dharma at the Inner Depot.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew still fonder of heterodox faiths, wore their robes, recited their scriptures, and preached at the Inner Depot.

sentences.zh: 綽吉我些兒輩出入豹房，與權幸雜處，氣焰灼然。

translations.literal: Chuoqi Wo'er and his kind came and went in the Leopard Quarter, mingling with the powerful and favored, their arrogance blazing.
translations.idiomatic: Chuoqi Wo'er and his circle moved freely in the Leopard Quarter with the powerful, their arrogance blazing.

sentences.zh: 及二人乘傳歸，所過驛騷，公私咸被其患。

translations.literal: When the two men returned by courier relay, every post station they passed was thrown into turmoil, and public and private interests alike suffered.
translations.idiomatic: When the two returned by courier relay, every post station they passed was thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 世宗立，復汰番僧，法王以下悉被斥。

translations.literal: When Shizong ascended the throne he again purged Tibetan monks; from Dharma King downward all were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong again purged Tibetan monks and dismissed all from Dharma King downward.

sentences.zh: 後世宗崇道教，益黜浮屠，自是番僧鮮至中國者。

translations.literal: Later Shizong honored Daoism and dismissed Buddhism still further; from then on Tibetan monks seldom reached China.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong later exalted Daoism and further suppressed Buddhism; Tibetan monks thereafter seldom reached China.

sentences.zh: 闡化王

translations.literal: The Taming King
translations.idiomatic: The Taming King

sentences.zh: 闡化王者，烏斯藏僧也。

translations.literal: The Taming King was a U-Tsang monk.
translations.idiomatic: The Taming King was a U-Tsang monk.

sentences.zh: 初，洪武五年，河州衛言：「烏斯藏怕木竹巴之地，有僧曰章陽沙加監藏，元時封灌頂國師，為番人推服。

translations.literal: At first, in the fifth year of Hongwu, Hezhou Guard reported: "In the land of Phagmodrupa in U-Tsang there is a monk named Zhangyang Shajia Jiancang, enfeoffed Abhisheka State Teacher in Yuan times and respected by the tribes.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 5 Hezhou Guard reported, "In Phagmodrupa in U-Tsang there was a monk named Zhangyang Shajia Jiancang, enfeoffed Abhisheka State Teacher under the Yuan and respected by the tribes.

sentences.zh: 今朵甘酋賞竹監藏與管兀兒構兵，若遣此僧撫諭，朵甘必內附。」

translations.literal: Now the Duo-Gan chieftain Shangzhu Jiancang is at war with Guan'uer; if this monk is sent to soothe and instruct them, Duo-Gan will surely submit inward.
translations.idiomatic: The Duo-Gan chieftain Shangzhu Jiancang was at war with Guan'uer; if this monk were sent to pacify them, Duo-Gan would submit.

sentences.zh: 帝如其言，仍封灌頂國師，遣使賜玉印、彩幣。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this advice, reconfirmed him as Abhisheka State Teacher, and sent envoys with a jade seal and patterned silks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, reconfirmed him Abhisheka State Teacher, and sent a jade seal and silks.

sentences.zh: 明年，其僧使酋長鎖南藏卜貢佛像、佛書、舍利。

translations.literal: The next year the monk sent the chieftain Suonan Zangbu to offer Buddha images, Buddhist texts, and relics.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he sent chieftain Suonan Zangbu with Buddha images, scriptures, and relics.

sentences.zh: 是時方命佛寶國師招諭番人，於是怕木竹巴僧等自稱輦卜闍，遣使進表及方物。

translations.literal: At that time the Radiant Buddha Treasure State Teacher had just been ordered to summon and instruct the tribes; the Phagmodrupa monks then styled themselves Gyalpo Khyab and sent envoys with a memorial and local products.
translations.idiomatic: As the Radiant Buddha Treasure State Teacher was summoning the tribes, Phagmodrupa monks styled themselves Gyalpo Khyab and sent a memorial with local goods.

sentences.zh: 帝厚賜之。

translations.literal: The emperor richly rewarded them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor richly rewarded them.

sentences.zh: 輦卜闍者，其地首僧之稱也。

translations.literal: Gyalpo Khyab was the title of the chief monk of that region.
translations.idiomatic: Gyalpo Khyab was the title of the region's chief monk.

sentences.zh: 八年正月設怕木竹巴萬戶府，以番酋為之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year the Phagmodrupa Myriad Households Office was established, with a tribal chieftain as its head.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighth year a Phagmodrupa Myriad Households Office was established under a tribal chieftain.

sentences.zh: 已而章陽沙加卒，授其徒鎖南扎思巴噫監藏卜為灌頂國師。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Zhangyang Shajia died, and his disciple Suonan Zhasiba Yijiancangbu was granted Abhisheka State Teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangyang Shajia soon died, and his disciple Suonan Zhasiba Yijiancangbu was made Abhisheka State Teacher.

sentences.zh: 二十一年上表稱病，舉弟吉剌思巴監藏巴藏卜自代，遂授灌頂國師。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he memorialized claiming illness and recommended his younger brother Jelisi Bazangbazangbu to replace him; Abhisheka State Teacher was then granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he memorialized illness and recommended his brother Jelisi Bazangbazangbu; the latter was made Abhisheka State Teacher.

sentences.zh: 自是三年一貢。

translations.literal: From then on tribute came once every three years.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute thereafter came every three years.

sentences.zh: 宣德二年命中官侯顯往賜絨錦、彩幣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuande the emperor ordered the eunuch Hou Xian to go and bestow velvet brocade and patterned silks.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 2 the eunuch Hou Xian was sent with velvet brocade and silks.

sentences.zh: 其貢使嘗毆殺驛官子，帝以其無知，遣還，敕王戒飭而已。

translations.literal: Their tribute envoys once beat to death a post official's son; the emperor, taking them as ignorant, sent them back and merely ordered the king to admonish them.
translations.idiomatic: Their envoys once beat a post official's son to death; the emperor sent them home and merely told the king to discipline them.

sentences.zh: 九年，貢使歸，以賜物易茶。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, as the tribute envoys returned, they exchanged granted goods for tea.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year returning envoys traded imperial gifts for tea.

sentences.zh: 至臨洮，有司沒入之，羈其使，請命。

translations.literal: At Lintao the local authorities confiscated the goods, detained the envoys, and asked for orders.
translations.idiomatic: At Lintao officials confiscated the goods, detained the envoys, and sought orders.

sentences.zh: 詔釋之，還其茶。

translations.literal: An edict released them and returned the tea.
translations.idiomatic: An edict released them and returned the tea.

sentences.zh: 正統五年，王卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengtong the king died.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 5 the king died.

sentences.zh: 遣禪師二人為正副使，封其從子吉剌思巴永耐監藏巴藏卜為闡化王。

translations.literal: Two Chan masters were sent as chief and deputy envoys to enfeoff his nephew Jelisi Bayongnai Jiancangbazangbu as Taming King.
translations.idiomatic: Two Chan masters were sent as chief and deputy envoys to enfeoff his nephew Jelisi Bayongnai Jiancangbazangbu Taming King.

sentences.zh: 使臣私市茶彩數萬，令有司運致。

translations.literal: The envoys privately purchased tens of thousands in tea and silks and ordered local authorities to transport them.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys privately bought tens of thousands in tea and silks and ordered officials to transport them.

sentences.zh: 禮官請禁之，帝念其遠人，但令自僦舟車。

translations.literal: Ritual officials asked that this be forbidden; the emperor, mindful that they were men from afar, only ordered them to hire boats and carts themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officials asked to forbid it; the emperor, mindful they came from afar, only required them to hire their own transport.

sentences.zh: 已，王卒，以桑兒結堅昝巴藏卜嗣。

translations.literal: Later the king died, and Sang'er Jiejianzan Bazangbu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: The king later died, and Sang'er Jiejianzan Bazangbu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 成化元年，禮部言：「宣、正間，諸貢不過三四十人，景泰時十倍，天順間百倍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chenghua the Ministry of Rites said: "Between Xuande and Zhengtong tribute parties numbered no more than thirty or forty; in Jingtai they were ten times that; in Tianshun a hundred times.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 1 the Ministry of Rites said, "Under Xuande and Zhengtong tribute parties numbered thirty or forty at most; under Jingtai ten times that; under Tianshun a hundred times.

sentences.zh: 今貢使方至，乞敕諭闡化王，令如洪武舊制，三年一貢。」

translations.literal: Now the tribute envoys have just arrived; we beg that the Taming King be instructed by edict to follow the old Hongwu rule of tribute once every three years.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute envoys have just arrived; we ask that the Taming King be instructed to follow the old Hongwu triennial rule.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 五年，王卒，命其子公葛列思巴中柰領占堅參巴兒藏卜嗣。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the king died, and his son Gonggelisi Bazhongnai Lingzhan Jiancanba'er Zangbu was ordered to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the king died, and his son Gonggelisi Bazhongnai Lingzhan Jiancanba'er Zangbu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 遣僧進貢，還至西寧，留寺中不去，又冒名入貢，隱匿所賜璽書、幣物。

translations.literal: A monk sent with tribute, on returning to Xining, stayed in a temple and would not leave; he also entered tribute under a false name and concealed the granted imperial letter, silks, and goods.
translations.idiomatic: A tribute monk stayed at a Xining temple on his return, entered tribute again under a false name, and hid the granted imperial letter and gifts.

sentences.zh: 王使其下三人來趣，其僧閉之室中，剜二人目。

translations.literal: The king sent three of his men to summon him; the monk shut them in a room and gouged out the eyes of two.
translations.idiomatic: The king sent three men to summon him; the monk locked them in a room and gouged out two men's eyes.

sentences.zh: 一人逸，訴於都指揮孫鑒。

translations.literal: One escaped and complained to Regional Commander Sun Jian.
translations.idiomatic: One escaped and complained to Regional Commander Sun Jian.

sentences.zh: 鑒捕置之獄，受其徒賄，而復以聞。

translations.literal: Jian arrested him and put him in prison, accepted a bribe from his disciples, and then reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian arrested him, took a bribe from his disciples, and reported upward.

sentences.zh: 下四川巡按鞫治，坐僧四人死，鑒將逮治，會赦悉免。

translations.literal: The case was sent to the Sichuan touring censor for trial; four monks were sentenced to death, and Jian was about to be arrested and punished, but an amnesty freed them all.
translations.idiomatic: The Sichuan touring censor tried the case; four monks were sentenced to death and Sun Jian was to be punished, but an amnesty freed all.

sentences.zh: 十七年以長河西諸番多假番王名朝貢，命給闡化、贊善、闡教、輔教四王敕書勘合，以防奸偽。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, because many tribes west of the Chang River falsely used tribal king names to come to court with tribute, edict letters and tally slips were ordered given to the four kings of Taming, Virtue-Praising, Propagation-Teaching, and Assistant-Teaching to guard against fraud.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, because many tribes west of the Chang River falsely used kingly titles in tribute, tally-bearing edicts were issued to the Taming, Virtue-Praising, Propagation-Teaching, and Assistant-Teaching kings to prevent fraud.

sentences.zh: 二十二年遣使四百六十人來貢，守臣遵新例，但納一百五十人。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year four hundred sixty envoys came with tribute; frontier officials following the new rule admitted only one hundred fifty.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year 460 envoys came; frontier officials under the new rule admitted only 150.

sentences.zh: 禮官以使者已入境，難固拒，請順其情概納之，為後日兩貢之數，從之。

translations.literal: Ritual officials, because the envoys had already entered the border and could not firmly be refused, asked to admit them according to circumstance and count them as two tribute quotas for later years; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officials said the envoys had already crossed the border and could not be firmly refused; they were admitted and counted as two future tribute quotas.

sentences.zh: 弘治八年遣僧來貢，還至揚州廣陵驛，遇大乘法王貢使，相與殺牲縱酒，三日不去。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Hongzhi monks were sent with tribute; on returning to Guangling Post in Yangzhou they met the Mahāyāna Dharma King's tribute envoys, and together slaughtered animals and drank freely for three days without leaving.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 8 tribute monks returning to Guangling Post in Yangzhou met the Mahāyāna Dharma King's envoys and feasted for three days without leaving.

sentences.zh: 見他使舟至，則以石投之，不容近陸。

translations.literal: When they saw another envoy's boat arrive, they threw stones at it and would not allow it near shore.
translations.idiomatic: When other envoys' boats approached, they threw stones and would not let them land.

sentences.zh: 知府唐愷詣驛呼其舟子戒之，諸僧持兵仗呼噪擁而入。

translations.literal: Prefect Tang Kai went to the post station, called out the boatmen, and admonished them; the monks, bearing weapons, shouted and swarmed in.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Tang Kai went to the post station to summon the boatmen and warn them; the monks, armed and shouting, surged inside.

sentences.zh: 愷走避，隸卒力格鬥乃免，為所傷者甚眾。

translations.literal: Kai fled to escape; only with clerks and soldiers fighting hard was he spared; those wounded were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Kai fled; only when his clerks and soldiers fought hard was he spared, and many were wounded.

sentences.zh: 事聞，命治通事及伴送者罪，遣人諭王令自治其使者。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, orders went out to punish the interpreters and escorts, and a man was sent to instruct the king to discipline his own envoys.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, interpreters and escorts were punished, and an envoy was sent to tell the king to discipline his own men.

sentences.zh: 其時王卒，子班阿吉江東答刂巴請襲，命番僧二人為正副使往封。

translations.literal: At that time the king died; his son Ban Ajijiangdong Daliba asked to succeed; two Tibetan monks were appointed chief and deputy envoys to go enfeoff him.
translations.idiomatic: The king had just died; his son Ban Ajijiangdong Daliba asked to succeed, and two Tibetan monks were sent as chief and deputy envoys to enfeoff him.

sentences.zh: 比至，新王亦死，其子阿往答刂失答刂巴堅參即欲受封，二人不得已授之，遂具謝恩儀物，並獻其父所領勘合印章為左驗。

translations.literal: When they arrived, the new king had also died; his son Awang Dalisi Daliba Jiancan at once sought enfeoffment, and the two men, having no choice, conferred it on him; he then prepared thank-offering gifts and also presented the tally seal his father had held as proof on the left.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they arrived the new king too was dead; his son Awang Dalisi Daliba Jiancan pressed for enfeoffment, and the two envoys, with no choice, granted it. He then prepared thank-offering gifts and presented his father's tally seal as proof.

sentences.zh: 至四川，守臣劾其擅封，逮治論斬，減死戍邊，副使以下悉宥。

translations.literal: Reaching Sichuan, frontier officials impeached them for unauthorized enfeoffment; they were arrested, tried, and sentenced to decapitation, commuted to exile on the frontier; all from deputy envoy downward were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: In Sichuan frontier officials impeached them for unauthorized enfeoffment; they were arrested and sentenced to death, commuted to frontier exile, while all from the deputy envoy down were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 正德三年，禮官以貢使逾額，令為後年應貢之數。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengde, ritual officials, because tribute envoys exceeded the quota, counted them as the next year's tribute allotment.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 3 ritual officials counted the over-quota tribute envoys against the following year's allotment.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年偕輔教王及大小三十六番請入貢。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiajing he came together with the Assistant-Teaching King and thirty-six large and small tribes to request entry with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 3 he came with the Assistant-Teaching King and thirty-six large and small tribes to request tribute entry.

sentences.zh: 禮官以諸番不具地名、族氏，令守臣核實以聞。

translations.literal: Ritual officials, because the tribes had not supplied place names and clan names, ordered frontier officials to verify and report.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officials, finding the tribes had not given place and clan names, ordered frontier officials to verify and report.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，闡化諸王遣使入貢請封。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year, the Taming kings sent envoys with tribute to request enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year the Taming kings sent envoys with tribute to request enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 禮官循故事，遣番僧二十二人為正副使，序班硃廷對監之。

translations.literal: Ritual officials following precedent sent twenty-two Tibetan monks as chief and deputy envoys, supervised by Clerk Zhu Tingdui.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officials followed precedent and sent twenty-two Tibetan monks as chief and deputy envoys under Clerk Zhu Tingdui.

sentences.zh: 至中途大騷擾，不受廷對約束，廷對還，白其狀。

translations.literal: Midway they caused great disturbance and would not submit to Tingdui's control; Tingdui returned and reported their conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Midway they caused great disturbance and refused Tingdui's authority; Tingdui returned and reported their conduct.

sentences.zh: 禮官請自後封番王，即以誥敕付使者齎還，或下守臣，擇近邊僧人齎賜。

translations.literal: Ritual officials asked that henceforth in enfeoffing tribal kings the patent and commission be given to envoys to carry back, or orders be sent to frontier officials to choose nearby monks to convey the gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officials asked that henceforth patents for tribal kings be given to envoys to carry back, or that frontier officials choose nearby monks to deliver them.

sentences.zh: 封諸藏之不遣京寺番僧，自此始也。

translations.literal: Not sending capital-temple Tibetan monks to enfeoff the various Tibetan regions began from this.
translations.idiomatic: From this time onward enfeoffment in the Tibetan regions no longer relied on capital-temple Tibetan monks.

sentences.zh: 番人素以入貢為利，雖屢申約束，而來者日增。

translations.literal: Tribal people have long taken tribute entry as profit; though constraints were repeatedly announced, arrivals daily increased.
translations.idiomatic: Tribes had long treated tribute as profit; despite repeated restrictions, arrivals only grew.

sentences.zh: 隆慶三年再定令闡化、闡教、輔教三王，俱三歲一貢，貢使各千人，半全賞，半減賞。

translations.literal: In the third year of Longqing it was again fixed that the three kings of Taming, Propagation-Teaching, and Assistant-Teaching should all tribute once every three years, each with a thousand envoys, half receiving full rewards and half reduced rewards.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing 3 the Taming, Propagation-Teaching, and Assistant-Teaching kings were again fixed to tribute triennially, each with a thousand envoys, half at full reward and half at reduced reward.

sentences.zh: 全賞者遣八人赴京，余留邊上。

translations.literal: Those receiving full rewards sent eight men to the capital; the rest remained on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Those at full reward sent eight men to the capital; the rest stayed on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 遂為定例。

translations.literal: This then became the fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: This became the fixed rule.

sentences.zh: 萬曆七年，貢使言闡化王長子札釋藏卜乞嗣職，如其請。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Wanli tribute envoys said the Taming King's eldest son Zhaxi Zangbu asked to succeed to the post; his request was granted as asked.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 7 tribute envoys reported that the Taming King's eldest son Zhaxi Zangbu sought succession; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 久之卒，其子請襲。

translations.literal: After a long time he died; his son asked to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: He died after a long reign; his son asked to succeed.

sentences.zh: 神宗許之，而制書但稱闡化王。

translations.literal: Shenzong granted it, but the commission only styled him Taming King.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong granted it, but the commission styled him only Taming King.

sentences.zh: 用閣臣沈一貫言，加稱烏斯藏怕木竹巴灌頂國師闡化王。

translations.literal: Following Grand Secretary Shen Yiguan's proposal, he was additionally styled Abhisheka State Teacher Taming King of Phagmodrupa in U-Tsang.
translations.idiomatic: On Grand Secretary Shen Yiguan's advice he was additionally styled Abhisheka State Teacher Taming King of Phagmodrupa in U-Tsang.

sentences.zh: 其後奉貢不替。

translations.literal: Thereafter tribute was offered without interruption.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter tribute continued without break.

sentences.zh: 所貢物有畫佛、銅佛、銅塔、珊瑚、犀角、氆氌、左髻毛纓、足力麻、鐵力麻、刀劍、明甲胃之屬，諸王所貢亦如之。

translations.literal: Tribute goods included painted Buddhas, bronze Buddhas, bronze pagodas, coral, rhinoceros horn, pulu felt, left-topknot horsehair tassels, zuli hemp, tieli hemp, swords, bright armor, and the like; what the various kings offered was similar.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute included painted and bronze Buddhas, bronze pagodas, coral, rhinoceros horn, pulu felt, horsehair tassels, hemp cloths, swords, and bright armor; the other kings sent much the same.

sentences.zh: 贊善王

translations.literal: The Virtue-Praising King
translations.idiomatic: The Virtue-Praising King

sentences.zh: 贊善王者，靈藏僧也。

translations.literal: The Virtue-Praising King was a Lingzang monk.
translations.idiomatic: The Virtue-Praising King was a Lingzang monk.

sentences.zh: 其地在四川徼外，視烏斯藏為近。

translations.literal: His territory lay beyond Sichuan's marches, nearer than U-Tsang.
translations.idiomatic: His territory lay beyond Sichuan's frontier, closer than U-Tsang.

sentences.zh: 成祖踐阼，命僧智光往使。

translations.literal: When Chengzu ascended the throne he ordered the monk Zhiguang to go as envoy.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzu took the throne he sent the monk Zhiguang as envoy.

sentences.zh: 永樂四年，其僧著思巴兒監藏遣使入貢，命為灌頂國師。

translations.literal: In Yongle 4 that monk Zhousi Ba'er Jiancang sent envoys with tribute and was appointed Abhisheka State Teacher.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 4 that monk Zhousi Ba'er Jiancang sent tribute and was appointed Abhisheka State Teacher.

sentences.zh: 明年封贊善王，國師如故，賜金印、誥命。

translations.literal: The next year he was enfeoffed Virtue-Praising King, the State Teacher title unchanged, and granted a gold seal and patent commission.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was enfeoffed Virtue-Praising King, kept his State Teacher title, and received a gold seal and patent.

sentences.zh: 十七年，中官楊三保往使。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the eunuch Yang Sanbao went as envoy.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year the eunuch Yang Sanbao was sent as envoy.

sentences.zh: 洪熙元年，王卒，從子喃葛監藏襲。

translations.literal: In Hongxi 1 the king died; his nephew Nange Jiancang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongxi 1 the king died and his nephew Nange Jiancang succeeded.

sentences.zh: 宣德二年，中官侯顯往使。

translations.literal: In Xuande 2 the eunuch Hou Xian went as envoy.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 2 the eunuch Hou Xian was sent as envoy.

sentences.zh: 正統五年奏稱年老，請以長子班丹監坐刂代。

translations.literal: In Zhengtong 5 he memorialized saying he was old and asked that his eldest son Bandan Jiancang succeed in his place.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 5 he memorialized that he was old and asked that his eldest son Bandan Jiancang succeed.

sentences.zh: 帝不從其請，而授其子為都指揮使。

translations.literal: The emperor did not grant his request but appointed his son Regional Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused the request but appointed his son Regional Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 初，入貢無定期，自永樂迄正統，或間歲一來，或一歲再至。

translations.literal: At first tribute had no fixed schedule; from Yongle through Zhengtong they came every other year or twice in one year.
translations.idiomatic: At first tribute had no fixed schedule; from Yongle through Zhengtong they came every other year or twice in one.

sentences.zh: 而歷朝遣使往賜者，金幣、寶鈔、佛像、法器、袈裟、禪服，不一而足。

translations.literal: Across reigns envoys sent with gifts brought gold coins, treasure notes, Buddha images, ritual implements, monastic robes, and Chan vestments in more than sufficient abundance.
translations.idiomatic: Across reigns imperial envoys brought gold coins, treasure notes, Buddha images, ritual implements, monastic robes, and Chan vestments in abundance.

sentences.zh: 至成化元年始定三歲一貢之例。

translations.literal: Not until Chenghua 1 was the triennial tribute rule fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Only in Chenghua 1 was the triennial tribute rule fixed.

sentences.zh: 三年命塔兒把堅粲襲封。

translations.literal: In the third year Ta'er Bajian Can was ordered to succeed and receive enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Ta'er Bajian Can was ordered to succeed and be enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 故事，封番王誥敕及幣帛遣官齎賜，至是西陲多事，禮官乞付使者齎回，從之。

translations.literal: By precedent patent and silks for enfeoffing tribal kings were sent by officials to bestow; now with many troubles on the western frontier, ritual officials asked that they be given to envoys to carry back; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent patents and silks for tribal kings were delivered by officials; with the western frontier in turmoil, ritual officials asked that envoys carry them back instead, and this was approved.

sentences.zh: 五年，四川都司言，贊善諸王不遵定制，遣使率各寺番僧百三十二種入貢，且無番王印文，今止留十余人守貢物，余已遣還。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the Sichuan Regional Military Commission reported that the Virtue-Praising and other kings did not follow the established rules, sending envoys leading Tibetan monks of one hundred thirty-two groups from various temples to tribute, and without tribal king seal documents; now only a dozen or so were kept to guard the tribute goods and the rest had been sent back.
